intro.title: Zustand for Global State
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple counter application to understand how to manage global state across your React components using Zustand. You'll learn the core concept of a centralized store, which allows multiple components to share and update the same data without prop drilling. The main technologies involved are React with TypeScript for building the UI and the Zustand library for creating and using the store. You'll implement a store with state and actions, and then connect your components to read from and write to that store. By the end, you'll have a working app that demonstrates clean, scalable state management.
intro.usecase: Zustand is commonly used in real-world React applications where multiple components need to share and update the same state across different parts of the UI. For example, in e-commerce dashboards, Zustand can manage shopping cart state that needs to be accessed by product listings, cart preview panels, and checkout modals simultaneously. It's also practical for user preference settings that affect UI themes, language selections, and layout configurations across an entire application. Developers use Zustand in admin panels to handle complex filter states that need to be synchronized between data tables, charts, and control panels without prop drilling.
